q0faa8535.question: Inline annotation is a JCEF-only affordance: on a JBR-without-JCEF the S002 native-editor fallback stays readable but cannot anchor comments. Whether the native fallback should offer a coarser whole-artifact (un-anchored) comment affordance, or annotation stays JCEF-only, is deferred — either keeps lc1/k6; flagged for the plan/build.
q0faa8535.rationale: User's decision (took the recommended default). Inline comments ship only in the JCEF view; the S002 native-editor fallback stays read-only and shows a one-line notice that annotation needs a JCEF-capable JBR. Smallest s3 surface (one authoring path, one anchor model). The sc3 CommentAnchor already has all fields optional, so a future coarse un-anchored native affordance remains a purely additive follow-up with no contract change.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Thin three-layer review surface over existing daemon capability; reasoning stays daemon-side (k1), the plugin only renders and transports. Phase B adds inline PR-style anchored comment threads.

boundary.internal: Private to s3: the inline-anchor UI mechanics, the JBCefJSQuery add/edit/remove-comment bridge, and the un-submitted, presentation-only comment buffer. No approval or resolution reasoning (k1).

ownedContracts.name: ReviewComment
ownedContracts.purpose: The inline-anchored comment model a reviewer builds while reading, plus the write contract that records those comments as open-question resolutions.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface CommentAnchor { readonly sectionPath?: string; readonly quote?: string; readonly openQuestionId?: string; }
interface ReviewComment { readonly id: string; readonly anchor: CommentAnchor; readonly body: string; }

consumedContracts.name: ArtifactReviewView
consumedContracts.purpose: The read-only view a reviewer sees; S003 overlays comments on its rendered content and reads openQuestions[].id.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — Inline annotation + submit as open-question resolutions

api.name: CommentBuffer
api.signature: class CommentBuffer { fun add(anchor: CommentAnchor, body: String): ReviewComment; fun edit(id: String, body: String): Boolean; fun remove(id: String): Boolean; fun snapshot(): List<ReviewComment>; fun clear() }

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.purpose: The captured target of a new comment (sectionPath/quote/openQuestionId) from the JS layer.

parameters.name: body
parameters.purpose: The reviewer's comment text (add) or replacement text (edit).

parameters.name: id
parameters.purpose: The client-generated ReviewComment id addressed by edit/remove.

returns.meaning: The pure Kotlin-owned un-submitted buffer (source of truth). add mints a client id + appends; edit/remove return whether the id was found; snapshot returns an immutable copy s4 reads at submit. Presentation-only — no persistence, no resolution reasoning (lc1/k1).

errors.condition: edit/remove of an unknown id return false (not an exception); the buffer never throws on normal ops.

preconditions: Holds only un-submitted comments; cleared or handed to s4 at submit.
postconditions: Mutation is in-memory only; the artifact and its .md/.json are never touched (k5).

api.name: ArtifactCommentLayer
api.signature: class ArtifactCommentLayer(buffer: CommentBuffer, browser: JBCefBrowser, parentDisposable: Disposable) { fun install(); fun onContentLoaded(view: ArtifactReviewViewDto); fun renderThreads() }

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.purpose: The Kotlin source-of-truth buffer this layer mutates from JS events and re-renders from.

parameters.name: browser
parameters.purpose: The S002 content-view browser whose page hosts the comment overlay (reused, not created).

parameters.name: parentDisposable
parameters.purpose: The tool-window disposable; the JBCefJSQuery objects register against it.

returns.meaning: The s3-owned comment layer hosted inside the S002 ArtifactContentPane: installs the JBCefJSQuery bridge + injects the comment JS, folds JS add/edit/remove events into the buffer, and re-pushes the current comment set to render anchored threads. Re-attaches on each content (re-)load so un-submitted comments survive a re-render.

errors.condition: a malformed JS payload is ignored (logged); the bridge never throws into the EDT.

preconditions: The JCEF surface is active (JBCefApp.isSupported()); in the native fallback the comment layer is inert (annotation is a JCEF-only affordance).
postconditions: JBCefJSQuery handlers are disposed with parentDisposable; no state persists past the panel.

api.name: JBCefJSQuery
api.signature: JBCefJSQuery.create(browser: JBCefBrowserBase): JBCefJSQuery; fun addHandler(h: (String) -> JBCefJSQuery.Response?); fun inject(jsResultCallback: String): String

parameters.name: browser
parameters.purpose: The S002 content browser the query is bound to.

parameters.name: h
parameters.purpose: The Kotlin handler receiving the JSON comment-op payload from JS.

returns.meaning: The external IntelliJ-Platform JS<->Kotlin bridge (consumed): JS calls the injected function with a serialized comment op; the Kotlin handler folds it into the CommentBuffer. In-process only (no socket/cloud).

errors.condition: create throws if the browser is disposed — guarded by the S002 disposed/isDisposed checks.

preconditions: Created at page-build time, before loadHTML injects the comment JS.

api.name: ArtifactContentPane
api.signature: internal class ArtifactContentPane(project, gateway, parentDisposable) { /* S002 + s3: hosts ArtifactCommentLayer, installs the bridge in composeHtml/render */ }

parameters.name: view
parameters.purpose: The sc2 view already rendered by S002; s3 reads its openQuestions[].id for open-question-targeted anchors and overlays the comment layer.

returns.meaning: The S002 pane (extended, not re-designed): composeHtml additionally injects the comment JS + the JBCefJSQuery inject() expression; render() wires the ArtifactCommentLayer to the freshly loaded page. The content fetch (s2) and pending list (s1) are untouched.

preconditions: Reuses the S002 JCEF/native surface + bundled renderer; annotation is active only on the JCEF card.
postconditions: No change to the sc2 fetch/render contract; the comment overlay is additive.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: S003 owns sc3 and realizes its comment MODEL: ReviewComment + CommentAnchor as Kotlin data classes, plus the pure CommentBuffer and the ArtifactCommentLayer that captures anchors via the JBCefJSQuery bridge and renders threads. The sc3 sketch's daemon WRITE portion (ResolveCommentRequest/ResolveCommentResult + the 'workflow.resolveComment' handler) is built by S004 (which consumes sc3); S003 defines the comment objects s4 submits and performs NO resolution reasoning (lc1/k1).

The comment layer overlays the sc2 content already rendered by S002: it anchors into that DOM and reads view.openQuestions[].id to set CommentAnchor.openQuestionId. It does NOT re-fetch (s2) or alter the sc2 contract; the small heading-id renderer hook is additive, not a re-design.

errorCases.scenario: A malformed comment-op payload arrives over the JBCefJSQuery bridge (bad JSON, missing op/anchor/body).
errorCases.detection: The Kotlin JBCefJSQuery handler JSON-parses the payload and validates op ∈ {add,edit,remove} + required fields; a parse failure or missing field is caught.
errorCases.response: Ignore the op (log at warn) and return a no-op Response; the buffer is unchanged and the current set is re-pushed to JS to re-sync.
errorCases.userImpact: The stray event does nothing; existing comments intact. No crash into the EDT.

errorCases.scenario: An edit/remove references a comment id not in the buffer (stale JS after a re-render, or a double-remove).
errorCases.response: Treat as a no-op and re-push the authoritative buffer to JS so the overlay re-syncs.
errorCases.userImpact: The overlay converges on the real state; no phantom edit/remove.

errorCases.scenario: The JBCefBrowser is disposed while a comment op / thread re-render is in flight (tool-window unload race, as in S002).
errorCases.detection: The S002 disposed flag + browser.isDisposed guard is checked before JBCefJSQuery.create / executeJavaScript.
errorCases.response: Skip installing the bridge / skip the re-render (try/catch); no exception escapes.
errorCases.userImpact: The panel tears down cleanly; no AlreadyDisposedException.

errorCases.scenario: An 'add' arrives with an empty anchor (no sectionPath, no quote, no openQuestionId) and/or an empty body.
errorCases.detection: The JS pre-checks a non-empty selection/target before posting; the Kotlin handler also rejects an all-null anchor or blank body.
errorCases.response: Do not add a ReviewComment; surface a subtle in-page hint; buffer unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: No un-anchorable/empty comment is created (keeps ac1/ac2 meaningful).

edgeCases.input: JCEF is unavailable so the S002 native-editor fallback is showing.
edgeCases.expected: Content still readable (s2 fallback), but inline annotation is inert — anchoring into a plain read-only text area is unsupported; the affordance is JCEF-only. No crash (documented limitation, consistent with k6).

edgeCases.input: A comment targets a rendered open-question marker.
edgeCases.expected: CommentAnchor.openQuestionId is set (from sc2 openQuestions[].id); the thread is anchored to that question and distinctly associated (ac2), ready for s4.

edgeCases.input: Several comments are added to the same section.
edgeCases.expected: Each is a distinct ReviewComment (distinct client id + its own quote) as its own thread — distinct association holds (ac2).

edgeCases.input: The page re-renders (poll refresh / re-open) while un-submitted comments exist.
edgeCases.expected: The Kotlin CommentBuffer survives; onContentLoaded re-pushes them and the overlay re-anchors by sectionPath/quote (ac3). An anchor that no longer resolves shows as 'unanchored', never silently dropped.

edgeCases.input: The reviewer switches to a DIFFERENT pending artifact.
edgeCases.expected: Comments are per-artifact; the buffer is scoped to the open artifactId (no cross-artifact bleed).

invariantsToPreserve.text: Un-submitted annotation state is presentation-only: the CommentBuffer holds comments in memory, performs NO approval/resolution reasoning, and nothing is persisted until s4's submit (lc1/k1).

A single artifact remains the single source of truth: comments are a SEPARATE annotation layer over the rendered content; the additive heading-id hook is a presentation aid — no divergent second copy (k5).

The one plugin artifact keeps loading across all four IDEs off the shared platform module; the annotation surface degrades gracefully where the embedded browser is unavailable (JCEF-only affordance; native fallback stays readable) (k6).
No cloud/REST path and no daemon write is opened by S003: the JS<->Kotlin bridge is entirely in-process, and the buffer is not submitted here (the daemon write is s4) (k2).

testLevels.purpose: Plugin: the pure CommentBuffer — add/edit/remove/snapshot/clear, headless (no JCEF).
subjects: CommentBuffer.add mints a client id, appends, and returns the ReviewComment carrying the anchor+body (ac1)
CommentBuffer.edit(known id) updates the body and is reflected in snapshot; edit(unknown id) returns false and changes nothing (ac3)
CommentBuffer.remove(known id) drops it from snapshot; remove(unknown id) returns false (ac3)
snapshot() returns an immutable copy in insertion order; clear() empties it
two adds to the same sectionPath get DISTINCT ids and each retains its own quote (ac2)

testLevels.purpose: Plugin: the pure comment-op applier (the JBCefJSQuery handler's core), headless.

applyCommentOp(edit/remove) by id -> reflected in snapshot (ac3)
malformed JSON / unknown op / missing fields -> no-op (buffer unchanged), no throw
an add with an all-null anchor OR a blank body -> rejected
an add whose anchor carries openQuestionId -> distinctly associated (ac2)

testLevels.purpose: Plugin: the ReviewComment/CommentAnchor model + per-artifact scoping.
subjects: CommentAnchor supports section-only, quote-only, openQuestion-only, and combined anchors (all optional)
the buffer is scoped per artifactId so switching artifacts shows only that artifact's comments

provingTests: CommentBuffer.add returns a ReviewComment carrying the anchor+body
applyCommentOp(add) with a valid anchor -> buffer gains the anchored comment
two adds to the same sectionPath get distinct ids + own quotes
an openQuestionId-anchored add is distinctly associated in snapshot
CommentBuffer.edit(known) reflected in snapshot; edit(unknown) -> false, no change
CommentBuffer.remove(known) drops it; applyCommentOp(edit/remove) reflected before any submit

testStrategy.testFramework: Plugin: JUnit5 (pure Kotlin units — CommentBuffer + the comment-op applier + the anchor model) via ./gradlew test on JDK21, mirroring S001/S002. No daemon test (S003 is plugin-only). The JS layer (heading-id hook, window.getSelection capture, JBCefJSQuery wiring, thread rendering) has no JVM harness — exercised manually + backstopped by the pure Kotlin core that owns all mutation; recorded as the known JS-untested residual (as in S002). No live socket, no GitHub CI.

migration.stateBefore: S002 (main 505a95f) ships the JCEF content view: ArtifactContentPane creates a JBCefBrowser and composeHtml inlines the bundled markdown-renderer.js + a bootstrap and loadHTML()s the rendered artifact into CARD_JCEF, with a read-only native fallback. The renderer emits headings WITHOUT ids. No comment/annotation code, no JBCefJSQuery use, no daemon comment IPC. renderedMarkdown is the single source of truth; the sc2 view carries openQuestions[].id.
migration.stateAfter: The plugin adds the sc3 comment MODEL + a pure CommentBuffer + an ArtifactCommentLayer hosted in ArtifactContentPane that installs a JBCefJSQuery bridge, injects a comment JS layer, folds add/edit/remove into the buffer, and re-renders anchored threads from the buffer. The bundled renderer is additively extended to emit heading ids. No daemon change; the buffer is presentation-only (submit is s4). All S002 behaviour unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the sc3 model (ReviewComment, CommentAnchor) + the pure CommentBuffer (add/edit/remove/snapshot/clear). Net-new.
Add the pure comment-op applier (parse {op, comment} JSON -> a CommentBuffer mutation, rejecting malformed/empty). Net-new; the JBCefJSQuery handler delegates to it.
Additively extend markdown-renderer.js: headings emit a stable id (slug + ordinal) + expose the heading path. Additive; escaping/link/CSP unchanged.
Add the comment JS layer (bundled resource): selection/marker 'add comment' affordance, anchor capture, thread rendering from the pushed set, and the injected JBCefJSQuery call for add/edit/remove.

Wire ArtifactCommentLayer into ArtifactContentPane: create the JBCefJSQuery(ies) at page-build time (guarded by disposed/isDisposed), install on the JCEF card only, and re-attach + re-push the buffer on each content (re-)load. Native fallback untouched.
Add the plugin JUnit tests (CommentBuffer, the comment-op applier, the anchor model + per-artifact scoping). Verify locally via ./gradlew test JDK21.

migration.backwardCompat: Fully backward compatible and purely additive: no existing public API changes. ArtifactContentPane's sc2 fetch/render contract is unchanged (the comment layer overlays it); the renderer change is additive (heading ids only) with escaping/link/CSP intact; no daemon IPC is added or altered (the submit write is s4). S001 + S002 behave exactly as before; a reviewer on a JBR-without-JCEF still reads via the native fallback (annotation inert). No cross-repo/IPC contract touched.

alternativesConsidered.name: Kotlin-owned buffer; JS captures anchors + renders threads via JBCefJSQuery; small additive renderer hook for stable section anchors
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The authoritative un-submitted ReviewComment buffer lives Kotlin-side (testable, s4-readable, survives re-render); the JCEF JS layer captures the anchor and posts add/edit/remove ReviewComment JSON through JBCefJSQuery; Kotlin updates the buffer and re-pushes state to render threads.
alternativesConsidered.approach: S003 defines the sc3 model as Kotlin types + a pure CommentBuffer (source of truth). ArtifactContentPane creates JBCefJSQuery handler(s) on the JBCefBrowser (disposed with it); composeHtml injects a comment JS layer that captures the anchor (sectionPath via a small additive renderer hook giving heading ids; quote = selected text; openQuestionId on a marker click) and posts a JSON op through the injected query. Kotlin folds it into the CommentBuffer and re-pushes the set to JS. Presentation-only (lc1/k1); s4 reads snapshot() at submit.
pros: Kotlin-side buffer: unit-testable without JCEF, s4-readable, and SURVIVES a page re-render (poll refresh won't drop un-submitted comments — ac3).
sc3 realized as first-class Kotlin types that s4 consumes directly.
Stable anchors (sectionPath heading id + quote) give distinct, re-locatable association (ac1/ac2); openQuestionId ties a comment to a question.
JBCefJSQuery is the standard, disposed-with-browser bridge.
cons: Two-way sync (Kotlin buffer <-> JS DOM) must stay consistent.
Needs a small additive hook in the s2-owned bundled renderer (heading ids) — back-flow-noted layering, not a re-design.

alternativesConsidered.name: JS owns the entire buffer; Kotlin pulls the ReviewComment[] at submit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The comment model + un-submitted buffer live entirely in the JCEF page's JS; Kotlin only executeJavaScript-pulls the ReviewComment[] at submit.
alternativesConsidered.approach: All add/edit/remove + anchoring + the buffer live in the page's JS; Kotlin holds no comment state; at submit s4 serializes the buffer out. sc3 exists only as a JSON shape.
pros: Simplest anchoring — the JS has the live DOM/selection.
cons: Un-submitted state lives ONLY in the browser: a re-render (poll refresh/re-open) DROPS all un-submitted comments — breaks ac3.
Un-unit-testable headlessly (JS with no harness) — the recurring least-covered/highest-risk trap.
s4 must reach into JS to read state (async executeJavaScript) — race-prone.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Loses decisively on ac3 (violates — un-submitted state is lost on any re-render) and is weak on sc3/k1 (JS-only model, untestable headlessly). Simpler anchoring does not offset losing the durability + testability of a Kotlin-owned buffer.

alternativesConsidered.name: Kotlin-owned buffer; anchors are quote+offset only, ZERO change to the s2 renderer
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same Kotlin-owned buffer as a1, but anchors are captured purely from the existing DOM (selected text + a computed section index) with NO additive hook in the renderer.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Kotlin holds the CommentBuffer (as a1). The JS derives CommentAnchor at capture time by walking the existing DOM (nearest preceding heading text -> sectionPath; selected text -> quote) without renderer ids. openQuestionId on a marker click. No touch to markdown-renderer.js.
pros: Zero change to the s2-owned renderer — cleanest boundary.
Kotlin-owned buffer keeps the a1 testability + re-render survival + s4-readability.
cons: Anchors are more fragile: without stable ids, sectionPath is recomputed from heading TEXT — duplicate/absent headings degrade to quote-only, weakening distinct association (ac2).
More anchor-derivation logic in untested JS.
Duplicate/absent headings make two same-section comments harder to tell apart (ac2).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Matches a1 except ac2 (partial): avoiding the renderer hook makes anchors heuristic (heading-text based), so multiple comments in the same/duplicate section are harder to tell apart and re-locate. The saved s2-touch is not worth the weaker distinct-association guarantee; the a1 hook is tiny and additive.
